## Purpose

Fixes #52846.

DeepSeek V4, V4.1 and V3.2 streamed a long string tool argument as one fragment when `</｜DSML｜parameter>` arrived. The configs set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so the engine skipped every plain body delta.

The fix now uses the per-parser `arg_value_extender` hook, the same way GLM (#61253) and Gemma4 (#61494) do. The earlier engine-level gate change is dropped.

- `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py`: `_dsml_arg_value_extender` returns an extender while the last parameter is an open `string="true"` value. Each delta streams as escaped JSON text without rerunning the converter. It stops on a parameter tag, keeping a tail so a tag split across deltas is caught.
- Wired into `deepseek_v4_config`, `deepseek_v32_config`, and `deepseek_v41_config` (spaced DSML tags via `functools.partial`).
- `_param_patterns`: the trailing-partial regex holds back an unfinished next `<｜DSML｜parameter` tag, so a streamed value never includes it (implicit close case).

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py`: `test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental` (4096-char body in 32-char chunks, needs >1 non-empty body delta and exact round-trip), `test_streaming_non_string_argument_is_withheld_until_close`, `test_streaming_string_argument_with_markup_is_incremental`.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::TestExtractToolCallsStreaming::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close`
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close` (spaced DSML)
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py::TestArgValueExtender` (split close tag, closed value, non-string value, repeated key)

Commands (CPU only):

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py

pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py

pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere

ruff check <changed files>; ruff format --check <changed files>
```

## Test Result

On this branch:

```text
deepseek v3/v31/v32/v4 tool parsers:  82 passed, 1 xfailed
engine + glm47 + gemma4 + v41 set:     589 passed
tests/parser + tests/tool_parsers:     7672 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed, 41 errors
ruff: All checks passed! / 6 files already formatted
```

The 41 errors are setup errors in `test_harmony.py` and `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py` (gated or unreachable HF downloads on my machine). `tests/parser/cohere` was skipped: `cohere_melody` is not installed.

Same new tests against upstream/main parser code:

```text
FAILED test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py::test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental - assert 0 > 1
FAILED test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::...::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 0 > 1
FAILED parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 2 > (4096 // 64)
```

V4, 4096-char body in 128 chunks: 0/128 body chunks emit arguments on main, 128/128 on this branch.

This looks like the correct direction after rebasing on top of the recent extender work merged for other models. Because this is a performance-sensitive PR, there's one quadratic regex added in this fix that I'd like us to fix just to not fix one performance problem but expose another. Let me know if you need help following what I pointed out there.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I believe this new regex is itself quadratic in time. It tries the optional `{start}[^>]*` branch at every `<｜DSML｜parameter` inside the value, and each attempt scans ahead to the next `>`. Both the converter and the extender factory run it on every conversion.

The lazy group plus `$` also causes a smaller bug: `$` matches just before a trailing `\n`, so for `...string="true">def f():\n` the check `pm.end(3) != len(raw_args)` is true and the extender never arms. Those deltas then go back to waiting for the next `>`.

My coding assistant suggested a fix like below for this to avoid the quadratic regex and take a test with 2,200 literal markers in one string value from 3.7 seconds for the converter + extender call down to 5 milliseconds on my machine.

Below is one suggested fix and analysis created by my coding assistant, but please review this suggestion and only copy it verbatim if it also looks good to you.

---

  Suggested fix: match greedily and do the holdback in Python. The holdback is the earliest `param_start` after the last `>`. That is exactly what the current regex selects, in O(n):
 
  ```python
  re.compile(rf"{head}(.*)\Z", re.DOTALL)  # trailing-partial regex
 
 
  def _match_open_param(
      raw_args: str, pos: int, partial_param_re: re.Pattern, param_start: str
  ) -> tuple[str, str | None, str, bool] | None:
      """Return ``(name, is_str, value, held_back)`` for the trailing open param."""
      pm = partial_param_re.search(raw_args, pos)
      if pm is None:
          return None
      value = pm.group(3)
      cut = value.find(param_start, value.rfind(">") + 1)
      if cut >= 0:
          return pm.group(1), pm.group(2), value[:cut], True
      return pm.group(1), pm.group(2), value, False
  ``` 
 
  The converter and `_dsml_arg_value_extender` both call this. The extender skips arming when `held_back` is true, which replaces the `pm.end(3)` check. `_dsml_arg_converter` takes a `param_start` kwarg, and `deepseek_v41_config` passes `DSML_PARAM_START` to it. I fuzzed this against the current regex on 200k inputs: results match except for trailing-`\n` inputs.

  Please also add tests for the holdback, which currently has no direct coverage:
  - V4: `_dsml_arg_converter(open + 'a > b<｜DSML｜parameter name="j', True)` returns `{"k": "a > b"}`, and the extender returns `None` for the same input.
  - V4.1: the same check through `deepseek_v41_config().arg_converter` with the spaced tags.
  - The extender arms for an open value ending in `"\n"`. This fails on the current head.

inline_comments.body:
I believe this new regex is itself quadratic in time. It tries the optional `{start}[^>]*` branch at every `<｜DSML｜parameter` inside the value, and each attempt scans ahead to the next `>`. Both the converter and the extender factory run it on every conversion.

The lazy group plus `$` also causes a smaller bug: `$` matches just before a trailing `\n`, so for `...string="true">def f():\n` the check `pm.end(3) != len(raw_args)` is true and the extender never arms. Those deltas then go back to waiting for the next `>`.

My coding assistant suggested a fix like below for this to avoid the quadratic regex and take a test with 2,200 literal markers in one string value from 3.7 seconds for the converter + extender call down to 5 milliseconds on my machine.

Below is one suggested fix and analysis created by my coding assistant, but please review this suggestion and only copy it verbatim if it also looks good to you.

---

  Suggested fix: match greedily and do the holdback in Python. The holdback is the earliest `param_start` after the last `>`. That is exactly what the current regex selects, in O(n):
 
  ```python
  re.compile(rf"{head}(.*)\Z", re.DOTALL)  # trailing-partial regex
 
 
  def _match_open_param(
      raw_args: str, pos: int, partial_param_re: re.Pattern, param_start: str
  ) -> tuple[str, str | None, str, bool] | None:
      """Return ``(name, is_str, value, held_back)`` for the trailing open param."""
      pm = partial_param_re.search(raw_args, pos)
      if pm is None:
          return None
      value = pm.group(3)
      cut = value.find(param_start, value.rfind(">") + 1)
      if cut >= 0:
          return pm.group(1), pm.group(2), value[:cut], True
      return pm.group(1), pm.group(2), value, False
  ``` 
 
  The converter and `_dsml_arg_value_extender` both call this. The extender skips arming when `held_back` is true, which replaces the `pm.end(3)` check. `_dsml_arg_converter` takes a `param_start` kwarg, and `deepseek_v41_config` passes `DSML_PARAM_START` to it. I fuzzed this against the current regex on 200k inputs: results match except for trailing-`\n` inputs.

  Please also add tests for the holdback, which currently has no direct coverage:
  - V4: `_dsml_arg_converter(open + 'a > b<｜DSML｜parameter name="j', True)` returns `{"k": "a > b"}`, and the extender returns `None` for the same input.
  - V4.1: the same check through `deepseek_v41_config().arg_converter` with the spaced tags.
  - The extender arms for an open value ending in `"\n"`. This fails on the current head.

     The ``string`` attribute is optional: the model sometimes omits it, and
     dropping such a parameter hands the client a tool call with no arguments.
+    The trailing-partial regex holds back an unfinished next parameter tag
+    so a streamed string value never includes it.
     """
     start, close = re.escape(param_start), re.escape(param_close)
     head = rf'{start}\s+name="([^"]+)"(?:\s+string="([^"]*)")?\s*>'

-        re.compile(rf"{head}(.*)$", re.DOTALL),
